# Quesar

> AI engineering engagements for traceable retrieval, bounded agent workflows, and private deployment.

## Site
- [Quesar by MLAI: Private AI operations](https://quesar.cloud/): AI engineering engagements for traceable retrieval, bounded agent workflows, and private deployment.
- [Abbey — Adaptive assistant on MLAI architecture](https://quesar.cloud/abbey): Abbey is the adaptive assistant experience on Quesar: a local document workspace and a CLI/TUI companion that will not claim what the ledger cannot prove.
- [Abbey bot — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/abbey-bot): Browser persona-routing illustration with an optional configured server model-request path.
- [ABI — Orchestration and inspectable context](https://quesar.cloud/abi): ABI is MLAI's local nightly Rust framework for routing assistant requests, assembling inspectable context, and reporting capabilities honestly.
- [About — MLAI Corporation](https://quesar.cloud/about): MLAI Corporation values, operating principles, and registration-level facts.
- [Apps — Quesar surfaces](https://quesar.cloud/apps): In-browser orientations of MLAI apps: Abbey workspace, mobile vault, Quasar studio, Abbey bot, plugins, and more.
- [Architecture — Quesar, ABI, WDBX](https://quesar.cloud/architecture): Interactive architecture of Quesar: user input, ABI orchestration, model routing, WDBX memory, provenance, and local or remote compute.
- [Benchmarks — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/benchmarks): Configuration facts, interactive models and workload notes. Not a borrowed scoreboard.
- [Cell machine — research automaton](https://quesar.cloud/cell-machine): Playable cellular automaton. Founder research, not a Quesar product surface.
- [Changelog — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/changelog): Release history for Quesar and the MLAI stack: the Rust-era milestones, with the superseded Zig history kept as an archive.
- [Abbey Companion — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/companion): Browser orientation to companion concepts. Native implementation and device acceptance require separate source evidence.
- [Company — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/company): MLAI: founder-led AI engineering, source references, implementation boundaries, and proposed engagement scopes.
- [Contact — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/contact): Discuss an MLAI engineering scope. The static preview requests an email draft; a configured server can accept an inquiry through the form.
- [Live demo — WDBX in-browser miniature](https://quesar.cloud/demo): Run an in-browser WDBX query-path miniature with cosine search over deterministic embeddings, an illustrative partition model, MVCC snapshots, and a…
- [Source — Quesar, ABI, WDBX, Abbey](https://quesar.cloud/developers): MLAI source orientation: repository metadata, README excerpts, setup requirements, verification gates, and site integrity rules.
- [Gama — founder Swift UI framework](https://quesar.cloud/gama): Gama is a modular declarative Swift UI framework. Founder-owned. Not a Quesar product claim.
- [Get started — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/get-started): Start journeys for research, Abbey, mobile, and Quasar without leaving this site.
- [Investors — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/investors): MLAI planning notes: illustrative financial assumptions, source reports, and proposed acceptance work.
- [Links — Quesar directory](https://quesar.cloud/links): Link hub and internal directory of Quesar pages and apps.
- [Mobile companion — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/mobile): Browser vault preview with localStorage notes and separate native shell source boundaries.
- [Platform — three layers, one chip](https://quesar.cloud/platform): Explore trace, control, evaluation, and runtime capabilities alongside the layers underneath them.
- [Plugins — ABI](https://quesar.cloud/plugins): Orientation to plugin and CLI concepts; synchronized installation requires separate source and acceptance evidence.
- [Privacy — Quesar / MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/privacy): How MLAI treats privacy as architecture: local processing, operator-owned memory, and the limits of this public website.
- [Quesar — model vision and assistant systems](https://quesar.cloud/quesar): Quesar is the model vision for Abbey, Aviva, and the assistant ecosystem. Explore current source, public orientation, and separately configured tools.
- [Security — Quesar / MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/security): Security posture for MLAI and Quesar: claim-honest language, local trust boundaries, and documented hazards.
- [Services — MLAI engineering](https://quesar.cloud/services): MLAI engineering services: audit, design, build, and harden AI systems that need traceability, private deployment, and operational control.
- [skill-creator — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/skill-creator): Browser composer for a SKILL.md preview and this site's integrity rules.
- [Terms — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/terms): Terms of use for the public Quesar orientation site. These terms cover the public website and in-browser app orientations.
- [WDBX — Provenance-aware memory substrate](https://quesar.cloud/wdbx): WDBX is MLAI's provenance-aware episodic substrate: durable records, vector retrieval, causal history, and inspectable evidence beneath ABI.
- [Abbey workspace — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/workspace): In-browser Abbey document workspace. The shipping app uses SQLite, a Python worker, and an optional local model.

## Products
- [Products — Quesar, ABI, Abbey, WDBX](https://quesar.cloud/products): Product journeys for ABI, Abbey, WDBX, and Quasar with availability and limits named.
- [Abbey — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/products/abbey): Explore a browser document workspace and its optional configured server model-request path.
- [ABI — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/products/abi): Explore deterministic persona routing, template completion, and source-defined tools.
- [Quasar — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/products/quasar): Generate a Next.js website and preview it on your own machine.
- [WDBX — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/products/wdbx): Store durable records and retrieve vectors with inspectable provenance.

## Docs
- [Docs — Quesar, ABI, WDBX](https://quesar.cloud/docs): Documentation for Quesar and ABI: getting started, runtime, personas, WDBX, MCP, and evidence.
- [Protected surfaces fail closed. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/api): The console requires a session. There is no public hosted assistant API.
- [Different tools. Clear roles. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/architecture): Separate runtime, storage, interface, and application framework responsibilities.
- [Each surface has its own gate. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/deployment): Packaging orchestration, retrieval, and controls. A web check is not mobile evidence.
- [Evidence before promises. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/evidence): Keep documented behavior, reported testing, measured results and targets separate.
- [One tree. Many surfaces. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/gama): A source-based introduction to Gama’s Swift scene and rendering model.
- [Start with the source. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/getting-started): Prepare an ABI checkout and follow its own validation workflow. Begin with the current ABI README and its toolchain and sibling-workspace prerequisites.
- [A companion, not a capability claim. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/identity): Understand Abbey, Aviva and ABI without confusing identity with implementation.
- [Twelve contract-covered tools. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/mcp): JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, optional loopback HTTP. Unknown tools fail closed.
- [Abbey, Aviva, Abi — profiles, not products. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/personas): Routing is a design mechanism. Per-persona quality is evaluated, not assumed.
- [ABI runtime, as the tree actually ships. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/runtime): Nightly Rust orchestration, wrappers, crates, and what a successful gate actually proves.
- [Fail closed. Tag the figure. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/trust): Sessions, evaluation gates, and the difference between measured, reported, and target.
- [Memory is a substrate, not a chat log. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/wdbx): Layered HNSW, MVCC, content addressing. Integrity of storage is not truth of the record.
- [The V2 snapshot, kept for reference. — Docs](https://quesar.cloud/docs/wdbx-v2): A frozen June 2026 documentation set from the earlier Abbey WDBX project. Not the current implementation guide.

## Research
- [Research — MLAI memory, retrieval, and orchestration](https://quesar.cloud/research): Research notes for MLAI and Quesar: memory architecture, retrieval, provenance, local inference, and implementation case studies with sources attached.
- [AI & agent behavior — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/ai-overview): Understand how Abbey and ABI route requests, produce local responses, and expose bounded checks. (published 2026-09-01)
- [Backtrace Confidence Signals for Hallucination Reduction — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/backtrace-confidence-signals-hallucination): A proposed study of whether visible evidence helps reviewers detect unsupported answers. (published 2026-02-01)
- [Chunk Provenance in Long-Context Retrieval Systems — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/chunk-provenance-long-context-retrieval): A proposed application pattern for preserving source references through document retrieval. (published 2025-11-01)
- [Evaluating Metal acceleration and CPU fallback — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/gpu-implementation-guide): Implementation guide: evaluating Metal acceleration and CPU fallback. Inspect native vector-operation support and explicit CPU fallback. (published 2026-09-01)
- [GPU & compute — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/gpu-overview): Inspect native vector-operation support and explicit CPU fallback. Assess whether a target Apple workstation can use the optional Metal DOT path. (published 2026-09-01)
- [Human Approval Gates That Operators Actually Use — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/human-approval-gates-operators-use): A proposed usability study for understandable approval and refusal flows. (published 2025-12-01)
- [Research implementations — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations): Nested MLAI implementation cases: platform layers, document pipeline, mobile vault, Quasar generation, Abbey claims, WDBX specimen, and research export.
- [Latency Budgets for Real-Time AI Orchestration — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/latency-budgets-real-time-orchestration): A proposed method for measuring the stages that determine interactive response time. (published 2026-03-01)
- [Connecting an MCP client to ABI — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/mcp-implementation-guide): Implementation guide: connecting an MCP client to ABI. Expose bounded ABI operations through a documented tool interface. (published 2026-09-01)
- [MCP integrations — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/mcp-overview): Expose bounded ABI operations through a documented tool interface. Evaluate a local integration from an MCP client into the ABI tool catalog. (published 2026-09-01)
- [Multi-Persona Routing Under Uncertainty: Policy Weights and Request Classification — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/multi-persona-routing-policy-weights): A corrected account of deterministic local profile routing and adaptive state in the SEA path. (published 2026-06-01)
- [Offline-First AI Workflows for Sensitive Data — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/offline-first-ai-sensitive-data): A bounded description of local deterministic processing and its evaluation uses. (published 2025-10-01)
- [Policy-Locked Tool Use in Multi-Agent Systems — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/policy-locked-tool-use-multi-agent): A proposed evaluation method for explicit authorization boundaries in agent workflows. (published 2026-04-01)
- [Prompt Injection Drills for Agentic Systems — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/prompt-injection-drills-agentic-systems): A proposed adversarial test set for agent boundaries and failure handling. (published 2025-09-01)
- [SEA evidence selection — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/sea-overview): Select a bounded set of relevant records before assembling an assistant context. (published 2026-09-01)
- [Sparse Evidence Attention for Bounded Context Assembly — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/sparse-evidence-attention-context-assembly): A source-backed account of eight-signal selection and bounded prompt assembly. (published 2026-06-01)
- [Using the local diagnostics dashboard and agent REPL — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/tui-implementation-guide): Implementation guide: using the local diagnostics dashboard and agent REPL. Inspect local runtime state and explore session-based agent interactions. (published 2026-09-01)
- [TUI & operator tools — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/tui-overview): Inspect local runtime state and explore session-based agent interactions. (published 2026-09-01)
- [Vector Index Maintenance Under Continuous Ingestion — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/vector-index-maintenance-continuous-ingestion): A source-based guide to persistence and index maintenance boundaries. Build document recall and decision-history prototypes with explicit source ownership. (published 2026-01-01)
- [WDBX Graph Weights for Traceable Neural Retrieval — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/wdbx-graph-weights-traceable-retrieval): Inspect how a candidate ranking can expose the factors that influenced it. (published 2026-05-01)
- [WDBX memory & retrieval — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/wdbx-overview): Durable records, searchable vectors and inspectable retrieval for applications that need continuity. (published 2026-09-01)
- [WDBX: A Weighted-Backtrace Memory Store for Traceable Retrieval — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/research/wdbx-weighted-backtrace-memory-store): A technical note on durable storage, approximate vector search and inspectable ranking, with legacy and canonical episode paths distinguished. (published 2026-06-01)
- [Abbey capability claims as an executable ledger — MLAI research](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations/abbey-executable-capability-ledger): Abbey centralizes capability statements in a typed registry whose status, evidence, dependencies, feature flags, and refusal behavior can be projected into…
- [Deterministic research exports with citation gates — MLAI research](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations/deterministic-research-provenance-exports): The Quesar research export pipeline converts validated publication records into stable JSON and static HTML, verifies and copies declared attachments, and…
- [Mobile Vault persistence across CloudKit and local fallback — MLAI research](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations/mobile-vault-cloudkit-local-fallback): The Quesar mobile Vault keeps one CRUD contract while selecting either the user's private CloudKit database or an encrypted local SecureStore fallback and…
- [A private document pipeline with explicit fallback behavior — MLAI research](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations/private-document-intelligence-pipeline): The private Quesar application implements bounded ingestion, workspace-scoped extraction and search, and consent-gated model access while making degraded…
- [Quasar as a bounded repository-generation loop — MLAI research](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations/quasar-bounded-repository-generation): Quasar couples an Anthropic tool loop to a narrowly constrained project filesystem, producing a local application through inspectable read, list, and write…
- [A six-layer architecture for evidence-aware AI systems — MLAI research](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations/six-layer-evidence-aware-platform): Quesar organizes interface, orchestration, retrieval, acceleration, storage, and audit as distinct layers so that evidence and runtime claims can be traced to…
- [WDBX Specimen separates architecture, runtime profiles, and proof — MLAI research](https://quesar.cloud/research/implementations/wdbx-specimen-architecture-and-conformance): WDBX Specimen combines a provenance-aware architecture specification with explicit browser and native runtime profiles, then uses conformance tests to make a…

## Blog
- [Blog — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/blog): Engineering notes from MLAI: memory, personas, privacy, and runtime discipline.
- [ABI Is Rust Now: What Changed, and What Didn't — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/abi-is-rust-now): The ABI runtime moved from Zig to a nightly-Rust workspace on July 30, 2026, and WDBX became its own sibling workspace in August. Here is what that means for… (published 2026-09-29)
- [Making AI Control Surfaces Feel Calm Under Pressure — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/calm-control-surfaces): Interface details that prevent overload: progressive disclosure, confidence bands, decision diffs, and emergency stop affordances. (published 2026-04-29)
- [Designing AI Systems That Can Explain Their Last Move — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/explainable-last-move): A practical guide to capturing retrieval paths, policy checks, and operator decisions so teams can debug autonomous workflows after the fact. (published 2026-05-21)
- [What Incident Reviews Need From AI Logs — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/incident-reviews-from-ai-logs): How to structure traces so teams can reconstruct context, model output, policy decisions, tool calls, and human overrides after a production event. (published 2026-04-18)
- [Inside the WDBX Hybrid Ranker: Four Factors, One Score — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/inside-wdbx-hybrid-ranker): Semantic similarity is only the first of four factors. Here is the exact score WDBX uses to rank retrieval candidates — and why every factor is bounded to… (published 2026-06-06)
- [Neural Backtracking: What a Block Chain Buys an AI Memory — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/neural-backtracking): Hallucination debugging is archaeology. WDBX chains every interaction block to its parent so you can prove nobody edited the record — and so a system can be… (published 2026-02-18)
- [On Saying “I'm Not Sure” — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/on-saying-im-not-sure): A note in Abbey's voice — the empathetic-polymath persona — on why an honest “I don't know” is one of the most useful things an agent can say. (published 2026-06-08)
- [Private AI Does Not Mean Invisible AI — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/private-ai-is-not-invisible-ai): Offline and VPC deployments still need measurable controls: local audit trails, release gates, repeatable evals, and operator-visible confidence signals. (published 2026-04-11)
- [What We Plan to Measure Before Calling an Agent Production-Ready — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/production-ready-agent-metrics): Latency and accuracy are not enough. The gate we are building tracks tool-boundary violations, source coverage, rollback paths, abstention quality, and… (published 2026-05-18)
- [The Case for Separate Planning, Review, and Execution Agents — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/separate-planning-review-execution): Role separation lets teams encode checks and balances into an AI workflow instead of relying on a single agent to police itself. (published 2026-05-08)
- [From Vector Search to Weighted Backtrace Graphs — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/vector-search-to-backtrace-graphs): Why retrieval infrastructure needs relationship-aware context and why ranking alone is not sufficient for high-stakes answer generation. (published 2026-05-12)
- [WDBX V2: Observable Memory, Multimodal Inputs, and Research Alignment — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/wdbx-v2-release): The second iteration of the WDBX runtime ships an observable pipeline: block-chain memory with temporal queries, multimodal input fusion, an async neural job… (published 2026-06-09)
- [The Weights Behind Abbey, Aviva, and Abi — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/weights-behind-the-personas): Persona routing is not a hidden model call. It is a normalized weight vector with hard policy overrides and an inspectable strategy decision. (published 2026-06-02)
- [How Sparse Evidence Attention Decides What the Model Sees — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/what-the-model-sees-sea): Before a model reasons, something must choose which records reach the context window. SEA scores eight criteria, then packs greedily under a hard token budget. (published 2026-06-04)
- [Why WDBX Is Written in Zig — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/why-zig): Garbage collection pauses are invisible in the mean and fatal in the tail. WDBX is Zig because a real-time vector database is a p99 product, not a p50 product. (published 2025-11-30; historical)
- [Surviving Writergate: Migrating ABI to Zig 0.16 — Blog](https://quesar.cloud/blog/zig-016-migration): Zig 0.16 rebuilt std.io around vtable-based Reader and Writer interfaces. Ninety-five files later, here's what the migration actually looked like — and the… (published 2026-01-08; historical)

## Projects
- [Projects — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/projects): Public project directory: ABI, WDBX, Abbey, and Gama with limits named.
- [Abbey — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/projects/abbey): The companion identity described in ABI’s source, with distinct interaction and governance roles.
- [ABI — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/projects/abi): Nightly Rust foundations for local AI orchestration, semantic storage, and explicit capability reporting.
- [Gama — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/projects/gama): A modular declarative UI framework in Swift, organized around scenes and a retained render tree.
- [WDBX — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/projects/wdbx): The semantic-storage work associated with ABI, with source-documented retrieval and persistence contracts.

## Team
- [Team — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/team): MLAI team: founder and systems architect Donald Filimon. Leads WDBX retrieval, the Abbey–Aviva–Abi orchestration framework, and the ABI runtime.
- [Donald Filimon — MLAI](https://quesar.cloud/team/donald-filimon): Building privacy-first AI infrastructure — durable memory, traceable retrieval, and bounded autonomy — close to the metal across Zig, Rust, and Swift.

## Source
- [Source — MLAI public tree](https://quesar.cloud/source): In-site catalog of public MLAI repositories. Each name opens a page here.
- [alien-invasion — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/alien-invasion): Real-time WebGL cinematic: seven chapters, one camera move.
- [Cell — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/cell-lang): Founder systems language: Rust ownership, Swift ergonomics, Zig control, compiled to a C ABI. Not a Quesar product claim.
- [cell-machine — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/cell-machine): Cellular-automaton experiment in Bun and TypeScript. Founder research, not a Quesar product.
- [cell-state — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/cell-state): Cell-state adaptive solver with a WebGPU lab simulation.
- [donaldfilimon — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/donaldfilimon): Profile and miscellaneous public work.
- [HydroCycle — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/hydrocycle): Founder hydrology experiment. Related by author, not a Quesar surface.
- [Invasion3D — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/invasion3d): Metal 4 renderer with SwiftUI and SwiftData. Founder graphics work.
- [mlai-py — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/mlai-py): Early Python machine-learning library sketch.
- [mlaix — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/mlaix): Private TypeScript sketch in the MLAI namespace.
- [NYON — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/nyon): A deterministic Rust strategy game with a separate offline Galaxy Workshop sandbox. A related source project.
- [ovo — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/ovo): Founder Zig experiment.
- [paint — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/paint): winit + wgpu + kurbo graphics app on Rust nightly.
- [donaldfilimon.github.io — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/portfolio): Personal Next.js static export. Separate from Quesar.
- [Star Space — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/star-space): Personal portfolio experiment. Not the company site.
- [wdbx-py — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/wdbx-py): Earlier Python WDBX implementation. The active substrate is the Rust tree.
- [wdnx — Source](https://quesar.cloud/source/wdnx): Earlier database specification work. Historical relative of WDBX.

## Showcase
- [Showcase — Quesar](https://quesar.cloud/showcase): Quesar showcase: trailer, film, explainer, design lab, Abbey, mega board.
- [Abbey — Showcase](https://quesar.cloud/showcase/abbey): The Abbey companion trailer. Persona language, not a capability claim.
- [Design lab — Showcase](https://quesar.cloud/showcase/design): The MLAI design lab: brand, system, showcase, hero, lab, marketing, console and docs boards.
- [Explainer — Showcase](https://quesar.cloud/showcase/explainer): What is MLAI? A narrated ~2-minute explainer. Vision is labeled, not asserted.
- [Film — Showcase](https://quesar.cloud/showcase/film): The full scene-library film on the shared timeline engine. Atmosphere, not a measured result.
- [Mega — Showcase](https://quesar.cloud/showcase/mega): The ~4.7-minute mega-trailer: kinetic beats and film scenes over a 3D neural field.
- [Trailer — Showcase](https://quesar.cloud/showcase/trailer): The 62-second MLAI vision trailer, rendered live in the browser. Orientation, not a benchmark.

## Quasar
- [New site — Quasar](https://quesar.cloud/quasar/new): Create a Next.js site from a prompt with your local Quasar service.
- [Settings — Quasar](https://quesar.cloud/quasar/settings): Set where this browser reaches your local Quasar service, and check that it answers.
- [Sites — Quasar](https://quesar.cloud/quasar/sites): Sites generated by your local Quasar service, read live from your browser.
